item.title: China-Russia-U.S. summit positive, constructive, fruitful: Xi
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 19:20:00
Photo: Xinhua Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that the China-Russia-U.S. summit has been positive, constructive and fruitful. Xi made the remarks while summarizing main consensus reached at the summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The three countries share the same view on safeguarding world peace, and all stressed that the hard-won peace must be cherished, Xi said. The three countries should follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, continue to strengthen communication, promote peace through cooperation, and work together to build a better world.

item.title: China unveils 34 new flagship enterprises to accelerate AI-driven transformation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 17:46:00
Dozens of UBTECH industrial humanoid robots carry out training tasks at a smart factory in the Qianwan New Area in Ningbo, East China's Zhejiang Province, on March 1, 2025. Photo: VCG China on Thursday unveiled 34 flagship smart factories across 20 provincial-level regions, expanding the initiative into more consumer-facing industries as the country steps up efforts to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) technology into manufacturing, boost productivity and accelerate the digital transformation of its industrial sector. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and five other departments released the 2026 flagship smart factory cultivation list, which includes major manufacturers such as Xiaomi Auto. Pharmaceutical and apparel manufacturers were included for the first time, highlighting the initiative's widening industry coverage. As the second batch of flagship smart factories, they have reported an average 34.4 percent increase in labor productivity and a 19.3 percent rise in production efficiency, while helping nearly 4,000 enterprises carry out digital and intelligent transformation in coordination. Notably, industry coverage has further expanded compared with the previous batch. Beyond equipment manufacturing, steel, electronic information and other fields, pharmaceutical and apparel enterprises in the consumer goods sector were included for the first time, according to the list released by the MIIT. The list includes smart factory projects from leading Chinese manufacturers across the vehicle, power equipment and shipbuilding sectors, including Xiaomi Auto, FAW-Volkswagen, Harbin Electric Machinery and Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding. The announcement by the six departments calls for supporting flagship smart factories in building high-quality industrial datasets, developing industrial AI agents, exploring advanced manufacturing models and establishing smart supply chains. The requirements highlight a broader shift in smart factory development, from equipment automation toward deeper integration of AI, industrial data and supply chain coordination. The MIIT announced 15 candidate factories on November 24, 2025, so the latest batch brings the total number to 49. Li Changan, a professor at the School of Public Administration at the University of International Business and Economics, told the Global Times on Thursday that the integration of AI with manufacturing is a major technological force driving the development of modern manufacturing. The inclusion of pharmaceutical and apparel manufacturers in the latest list shows that AI technologies are expanding beyond a limited number of industries and becoming increasingly integrated into traditional manufacturing sectors, according to Li. The expert further noted that the list not only reflects the progress of AI applications in manufacturing, but also serves as a demonstration and a model for the wider industry, encouraging more traditional manufacturers to accelerate technological upgrades and transformation. This trend is expected to further strengthen China's manufacturing capabilities, improve product quality and enhance the global competitiveness of its manufacturing sector. China has been accelerating the development of smart manufacturing. As of the end of June, the country had more than 56,000 basic-level, 9,000 advanced-level and 500 excellence-level smart factories, according data released in October, highlighting the expanding scale of its manufacturing digitalization drive China is stepping up efforts to integrate AI into industrial production. Under an action plan released in January, the country aims to develop 1,000 high-level industrial AI agents and 100 high-quality industrial datasets by 2027, while promoting AI applications across manufacturing. The expansion of flagship smart factories is expected to help turn technological advances into practical industrial applications and extend productivity gains across supply chains.

item.title: Xi makes four points on how major countries should get along with each other
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 17:45:00
Photo: Xinhua Photo: Xinhua Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace. Major countries should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation, Xi said at a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Xi said that countries should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respect the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and respect each other's core interests and major concerns. They should not interfere in other countries' domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs, he said. On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another, Xi said. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should be partners and friends. They should not go for conflict or confrontation among themselves, but should hold the line on peaceful coexistence and make efforts to avoid the Thucydides Trap. As the main victors of World War II, China, Russia and the United States should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, Xi said. He said that nuclear weapons, the Sword of Damocles that hangs over humanity, should be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of nuclear weapons. He emphasized the importance of win-win cooperation. The three countries should strengthen economic cooperation and trade, combine their respective strengths as major countries in resources, manufacturing and consumption, so as to make the pie of cooperation bigger and achieve win-win and all-win outcomes. Decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains are not the way to go. Xi said that the three countries could strengthen communication and coordination to safeguard the security and stability of the global energy market. He said that the three countries should maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep dialogue channels open at all levels, and establish crisis communication and prevention mechanisms to ensure that misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means.

item.title: China-ROK FTA upgrade set to boost bilateral travel: business insiders
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 16:22:00
Chinese tourists arrive at Incheon Port International Passenger Terminal in Incheon, South Korea, preparing to spend the May Day holidays from May 1 to 5, on April 30, 2026. Photo: VCG China and South Korea have substantially concluded the second phase of negotiations on the China-ROK Free Trade Agreement (FTA), which upgraded the investment, trade in services, financial services and economic cooperation chapters and related annexes of the original FTA. Business insiders said that the upgrade will give fresh momentum to the tourism, retail, entertainment and other services industries. Travel agencies in both countries told the Global Times on Thursday that they welcomed the progress, noting that they are expected to benefit significantly. Shares of South Korean travel companies rose during Thursday trading after the two sides concluded follow-up FTA negotiations on services and investment, according to South Korea's Chosun Biz. The rally was partly driven by expectations that South Korean travel agencies would be able to recruit outbound tourists directly in China, the report said. The second phase of negotiations on the China-South Korea FTA has been substantially concluded, with the investment, trade in services, financial services and economic cooperation chapters, as well as related annexes of the original FTA upgraded, according to a statement released by the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) on Wednesday. The agreement will further raise the level of liberalization and facilitation in investment and services trade between the two countries, and adopt a negative list approach for investment, cross-border services and financial services, the ministry said. It added that the agreement will create more transparent, stable and predictable market access rules for two-way investment and trade in services. The conclusion of the second phase of negotiations will create new opportunities for enterprises in both countries, consolidate the foundation of bilateral economic and trade cooperation, and inject fresh impetus into the steady development of the China-South Korea strategic cooperative partnership, a MOFCOM official said. Industry observers said that the completion of the talks could open new opportunities for travel agencies and other services providers in both countries, especially as China and South Korea continue to ease visa policies and expand people-to-people exchanges. A representative of Sun International Travel, Jenny Sun, told the Global Times on Thursday that the agreement would help the company expand its business in China. The South Korea-based travel agency specializes in serving Chinese tourists visiting South Korea. "Once the agreement takes effect, we will be able to recruit group tourists in China for trips to South Korea and sell travel packages. We will be able to expand our business by selling packages in China that combine tourism with K-pop and beauty offerings, as well as packages for travel to Japan and Southeast Asia," Sun said. She added that the company is also preparing to develop more itineraries to China for South Korean tourists and hopes to gradually expand its operations from one-way inbound services to two-way tourism cooperation. "Chinese tourists' demand is changing. More visitors now care about quality, personalized experiences and the overall comfort of the journey," Sun said, adding that the company is considering developing culturally themed products for South Korean tourists, such as Silk Road tour packages, with early interest in destinations including Xi'an in Northwest China's Shaanxi Province, and Dunhuang and Jiayuguan in Northwest China's Gansu Province. Sun said that over the next three to five years, the greatest opportunity in the China-South Korea tourism market lies in its gradual transformation from traditional sightseeing to immersive travel experiences, business exchanges, tailored tours, and two-way tourism cooperation. Another South Korean industry insider told the Global Times on Thursday that his priorities were easier market access for cross-border tourism services, simpler qualification requirements and fewer restrictions on travel agency cooperation. At present, outbound travel bookings to South Korea are dominated by independent travel, which accounts for more than 70 percent of total bookings. Demand is driven mainly by younger travelers and short weekend trips. Group tours represent a smaller share, consisting largely of senior sightseeing packages, study tours and business delegations, although bookings have been recovering steadily. The next phase of growth in China-South Korea tourism is likely to come first from young travelers, followed by silver-haired wellness and sightseeing tours, he added. With the agreement in place, he said that bilateral tourist flows would gradually recover to about 70 percent to 80 percent of pre-pandemic levels within one to two years. Chinese travel industry insiders also said that they expect the agreement to support outbound travel to South Korea, particularly as visa facilitation continues to improve. Xu Xiaolei, a marketing manager at CYTS Tours Holding Co, told the Global Times on Thursday that the agreement would likely encourage more Chinese travelers to visit South Korea. Xu said that bilateral tourism ties are already recovering, supported by favorable policies, improved transport links, warmer market sentiment and growing demand for cross-border cultural and leisure experiences. "The updated rules could also strengthen cooperation in retail, entertainment, digital services and other sectors tied closely to tourism demand," he noted. China began granting visa-free access to South Korean citizens in November 2024, a policy that has significantly boosted interest in travel to China. Shanghai has emerged as a particularly popular destination for South Korean travelers. With the visa-free dividend continuing to be released, South Korea has become Shanghai's largest source of inbound visitors. Data from local authorities showed that in the first half of this year, Shanghai received 5.31 million inbound tourists, with South Korean visitors accounting for nearly 10 percent, according to media reports. Meanwhile, South Korea has extended a visa-fee policy for group tourists from China, Vietnam and several other countries through December 31, according to South Korean media outlets. Official data showed that about 790,000 foreign visitors entered South Korea on group visas last year, up 39 percent year-on-year, with growth mainly driven by travelers from China and Southeast Asia.

item.title: Global conference on reproductive genetics held in Bangkok
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 08:18:00
The opening ceremony of the 2026 annual conference of the International Society of Reproductive Genetics (ISRG) is held in Bangkok, Thailand, Nov. 16, 2026. The 2026 annual conference of the International Society of Reproductive Genetics (ISRG) was held in Bangkok, Thailand, from Sunday to Tuesday. Hosted by the ISRG, the conference brought together experts and scholars from around the world in reproductive medicine, genetics and related interdisciplinary fields. They engaged in in-depth discussions on cutting-edge research, technological innovation and clinical translation in reproductive genetics, exploring new pathways for collaborative innovation and cooperation in the global reproductive health industry. (Xinhua/Sun Weitong) The 2026 annual conference of the International Society of Reproductive Genetics (ISRG) was held in Bangkok, Thailand, from Sunday to Tuesday. Hosted by the ISRG, the conference brought together experts and scholars from around the world in reproductive medicine, genetics and related interdisciplinary fields. They engaged in in-depth discussions on cutting-edge research, technological innovation and clinical translation in reproductive genetics, exploring new pathways for collaborative innovation and cooperation in the global reproductive health industry. ISRG President Qiao Jie, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, stressed in her opening remarks that the ultimate value of scientific research lies in whether it can make a tangible difference for patients. Looking ahead, she noted that research should leverage technologies such as single-cell genomics to deepen understanding of the mechanisms underlying gametogenesis and embryonic development. At the same time, rigorous, evidence-based studies are needed to validate the accuracy and reliability of genetic testing and to demonstrate its clinical benefits. She also called for greater promotion of multicenter research and exchanges among young researchers. Nijasri C. Suwanwela, associate dean for Academic Services & International Education at the Faculty of Medicine, Chulalongkorn University in Thailand, said that reproductive genetic issues concern people in all countries and represent a shared need. She expressed the hope that the conference would help strengthen genetic healthcare services, professional training, and international cooperation. Xie Xiaoliang, a member of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and director of the Changping Laboratory, highlighted research advances in non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing (niPGT) based on cell-free DNA in embryo culture media. According to Xie, the Changping Laboratory originally developed the core technology behind this achievement. By linearly amplifying the genome, the approach significantly improves the sensitivity and accuracy of non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing, enabling precise identification of genomic sequences in an embryo inherited from its paternal grandfather, paternal grandmother, maternal grandfather or maternal grandmother. Xie also believed the technology has promising application prospects. It could first be validated in families affected by thalassemia to assess its sensitivity and specificity, before being gradually incorporated into routine assisted reproductive procedures. It could serve as a "preferred low-risk option" or provide "supplementary evidence when biopsy results are inconclusive." The ISRG was established in Beijing in 2019 to provide a platform for scientific research, clinical exchange, and collaboration. The International Society of Reproductive Genetics (ISRG) President Qiao Jie, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, addresses the opening ceremony of the 2026 annual conference of the ISRG in Bangkok, Thailand, Nov. 16, 2026. Hosted by the ISRG, the conference brought together experts and scholars from around the world in reproductive medicine, genetics and related interdisciplinary fields. They engaged in in-depth discussions on cutting-edge research, technological innovation and clinical translation in reproductive genetics, exploring new pathways for collaborative innovation and cooperation in the global reproductive health industry. item.title: The Asia-Pacific is a realm for shared devt, a stage for co-op side by side: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 00:34:00
The APEC "China Year" logo decoration is seen at Qianhai Stone Park in Shenzhen. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19, 2026. Photo: Xinhua Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday delivered a keynote speech titled "Forging Ahead with Resolve, Toward a Bright Future for the Asia-Pacific" at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province. In the speech, the Chinese leader provided an in-depth explanation of the right path for the Asia-Pacific region to navigate the profound global changes unseen in a century, and clearly outlined the vast opportunities for cooperation that China's 15th Five-Year Plan will bring to the Asia-Pacific and the world. The address drew an enthusiastic response; attendees noted that it charted a course toward shared prosperity in the Asia-Pacific and further bolstered the confidence of the region's business community in achieving mutually beneficial cooperation. The Asia-Pacific is the most dynamic region in the global economy and a primary engine of growth, as well as a hub for innovation and openness. At present, the international landscape is fraught with turbulence and complexity; global economic growth lacks sufficient momentum, while unilateralism and protectionism are on the rise. Meanwhile, global trade has demonstrated resilience despite these headwinds, and breakthroughs in emerging technologies - such as artificial intelligence and green, low-carbon solutions - are accelerating, profoundly reshaping the global division of labor and the landscape of world development. What has happened to the world, and what path should the Asia-Pacific take? Should we choose openness or closure, cooperation or fragmentation, change or stagnation? The eyes of the world are turned toward the Asia-Pacific, and the region's expectations are focused on China. China has put forward four proposals for building an Asia-Pacific community and fostering shared prosperity in the region: uphold peace and stability, build bridges of opening up and cooperation, boost innovation to drive growth, and expand our ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. These four proposals represent the "right choice" for the Asia-Pacific as it navigates a period of profound changes unseen in a century. They are grounded in the practical needs of the region's current stage of development while aligning with the long-term trajectory of global economic transformation, effectively charting a clear, reliable course for all parties in the Asia-Pacific to follow amid turbulent times. Within this substantial agenda, the opening-up dividends unleashed by China's 15th Five-Year Plan present a significant opportunity that has captured the attention of the Asia-Pacific region and the world at large. China is the world's second-largest consumer market and home to the world's largest middle-income group. Ranging from the semi-conductor, the new-energy vehicle sector and biomedicine to the broad expansion of emerging fields such as smart home technology, the silver economy and winter sports tourism, the comprehensive expansion of China's high-tech and high-value-added sectors creates brand-new opportunities for high-quality goods and services from economies across the Asia-Pacific. Through measures such as the steady reduction of tariffs, the expansion of market access, and ongoing, in-depth exploration of "institutional opening-up" - encompassing rules, regulations, management, and standards - China is fostering a more stable and predictable environment for global enterprises to invest and thrive. Regardless of how the international landscape may shift, China's commitment to mutually beneficial cooperation with the world remains steadfast. The Shenzhen initiative of the APEC CEO Summit 2026, released during the summit, marks the first time in the 30-year history of the APEC CEO Summit that an outcome document has been issued in the form of an initiative. From deepening an open regional economy to driving inclusive growth through technological innovation, and from streamlining the arteries of regional integration to working together toward shared prosperity - these four priority areas outline the collective aspirations of the Asia-Pacific business community for regional cooperation, while offering a fresh approach to collaboration amidst a complex and ever-changing international economic landscape. The world is focused on Shenzhen, where a series of significant meetings are unfolding, and long-gestating cooperative concepts are being transformed into actionable, implementable plans. Inside and outside the venue, political and business leaders from the Asia-Pacific region and beyond are gathering to discuss pressing issues - such as connectivity, artificial intelligence, sustainable development, the construction of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, and the digital economy - sharing their perspectives and proposing concrete, practical solutions. Many corporate representatives arrived with carefully prepared lists of potential collaborations, utilizing even their coffee breaks for multiple rounds of engagement to swiftly identify new partnership opportunities. Standing at a new starting point for Asia-Pacific cooperation, the coastal city of Shenzhen is fully leveraging its role as a pivotal platform for fostering consensus and pooling collective strength. APEC emerged alongside the wave of economic globalization, propelling the Asia-Pacific region to the forefront of the times. Every step forward in Asia-Pacific cooperation has been driven by a firm commitment from all parties to work together side by side. The consensus reached today in Shenzhen marks a fresh departure point for the Asia-Pacific region to navigate through storms and challenges together. As the proposals put forward and the commitments made during this meeting are translated into concrete action, the vision and blueprint for an Asia-Pacific community will gradually become a reality of common prosperity, infusing a vital sense of certainty into an otherwise turbulent and unsettled world.

item.title: New Homo erectus fossils from two caves in Guangxi offer fresh clues to human evolution in China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 00:00:00
Illustration of the ancient human tooth fossils found in Baxian Cave and Naxian Cave. Credit: Courtesy of the research group Scientists from China and abroad have confirmed that eight of nine fossils of ancient human teeth discovered from the Baxian Cave and Naxian Cave in Chongzuo city, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, southern China, belong to Homo erectus . The fossils date to between 324,000 and 184,000 years ago and represent the latest known Homo erectus fossil record in China. The study was a joint effort by Zhang Yingqi, a research professor of the Research Team for the Cultural Evolution and Environmental Adaptation of Ancient Humans in East Asia, the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and scientists from more than 10 research institutions from six countries, including Shandong University. The research was published in Nature as two sister papers on Thursday. The Baxian Cave was discovered and studied by the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, while the Naxian Cave was discovered by the Anthropology Museum of Guangxi and studied by Shandong University. The two sites have yielded a total of nine ancient human teeth fossils. Through morphological analyses, the scientists identified eight of the nine teeth as belonging to Homo erectus , with the exception of the specimen PA1796 from Baxian Cave. Additionally, scientists found that the ancient humans from the two caves, except for specimen PA1796, were genetically associated with Homo erectus but belonged to a distinct population separate from other Middle Pleistocene groups in East Asia, including those found at Zhoukoudian in Beijing and He county in Anhui Province. The team said this identification was the most likely based on current knowledge and technology. Most known Homo erectus fossil sites in China are concentrated in the northern and central regions, with all previously discovered fossils dating back more than 400,000 years. The research team used five independent dating methods to establish the age of sediments and associated mammalian fossils from the two caves, which helped determine the age of the Homo erectus remains. Based on the dating results from the two caves, it can be concluded that Homo erectus lived in the Chongzuo area between 324,000 and 184,000 years ago. These fossils represent the latest known Homo erectus remains in China, challenging previous understandings of the species' survival timeline and geographical range. The discovery also establishes Chongzuo as a key area for investigating the extinction of Homo erectus in China. Analyses of associated mammalian fossils and tooth enamel isotopes suggest that Homo erectus could move over long distances through dense rainforests, challenging the long-held view that the species was confined to open savannas and woodland environments. These findings indicate that the Homo erectus fossils from Baxian Cave and Naxian Cave extend the species' known geographical and chronological range across mainland Asia. Homo erectus and Denisovans may have coexisted in southern Asia, with overlapping time ranges and neighboring geographic distribution. Chongzuo is therefore a key area for studying the evolution, interaction, and admixture of multiple archaic human lineages in the same region, as in East Asia more broadly.

item.title: GT Voice: Can China's chips power its AI boom? Telecom tender offers clues
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 23:36:00
A technician conducts chip quality inspections in a factory in Yiwu, East China's Zhejiang Province, in March 2026. Photo: VCG Can China's homegrown technology stand up to the demands of its expanding artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure? According to media outlet CWW, China Telecom issued a tender recently for equipment for its 2026 intelligent computing supernode clusters. The project offers a real-world test of how far China's AI computing capabilities have advanced. As China's AI industry expands, its telecom operators are stepping up investment in computing infrastructure, with supernodes becoming an increasingly important part of the country's intelligent computing architecture. China Telecom explained in a 2025 article that a supernode combines AI chips housed in multiple servers into a large computing unit through high-speed interconnects. International debate over whether US chips and technology are being used in China's AI development has intensified in recent weeks. Rather than give credence to unsubstantiated speculation, a more grounded assessment should focus on what is actually being deployed in China's AI infrastructure, which companies are supplying the equipment and technologies, and how well their products perform in real-world applications. China Telecom's procurement could offer a glimpse of what is actually happening on the ground in China's AI industry. According to CWW, the tender covers an estimated 5,248 intelligent computing servers, among other equipment. It calls for two server configurations and sets high technical thresholds for GPU computing power and other performance parameters, with the systems designed to handle computationally intensive workloads such as large-language model training and high-concurrency inference. The tender allows for up to five suppliers to win contracts. Whoever they are, the procurement process offers a window into a broader reality: China's AI infrastructure development is far from opaque. This is not unique to China Telecom. Many Chinese companies publicly disclose procurement notices and bidding procedures, giving outside observers ample information to understand how the country's AI infrastructure is being built. The information is there for anyone willing to look. Yet some overseas commentators seem determined to look the other way, continuing to speculate about China's so-called dependence on US chips, or even claiming that it has resorted to smuggling them. Such narratives reveal little about China's AI development, but far more about the arrogance of those advancing them and the political agendas they serve. So, can China's homegrown chips support the development of its AI industry? There is no shortage of real-world examples. At an intelligent computing center in Wuxi, East China's Jiangsu Province, 2,000 units of the Moore Threads MTT S5000 are now running close to full capacity. Designed for generative AI workloads, the MTT S5000 is a full-featured GPU accelerator for large-language model training, inference and high-performance computing, powered by Moore Threads' next-generation PH100 chip. China's AI industry is expanding at a remarkable pace, requiring enormous quantities of chips to power its growth. Does anyone seriously believe that an industry developing on this scale could be powered by "smuggled US chips?" The notion is not just implausible; it is frankly absurd. Anyone making such claims seems to have little understanding of the sheer scale of China's AI development. China's drive for technological self-reliance is making steady progress. The rapid expansion of its AI infrastructure and the development of domestic large-language models show that homegrown chips are increasingly capable of supporting the country's AI industry. The most reliable way to assess China's technological capabilities is to look at what companies are actually buying, which suppliers are winning contracts and how their products perform in real-world applications. These facts offer far more insight than speculation abroad driven by political agendas. China's AI industry is still evolving, and so is its homegrown chip sector. China Telecom's latest tender points to the scale of demand emerging in the market. That demand means more orders, more revenue for research and development and stronger incentives for suppliers to improve their products. As China's AI industry grows, it is also creating the market conditions for its homegrown chipmakers to advance.

item.title: Shenzhen APEC: an opportunity for Taiwan region to rediscover Chinese mainland
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 21:32:00
This photo taken on November 16, 2026 shows a view of Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province with APEC elements. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. Photo: VCG Some local news coverage in Taiwan region often portrays the Chinese mainland as being in a state of "economic collapse." Yet along the Pearl River in Shenzhen, bright lights stream across the skyline and traffic flows nonstop, embodying a city brimming with innovative vitality. Both refer to the same Chinese mainland. Why, then, are the pictures so strikingly different? A remark made during a cross-Straits media program held around the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen is worth reflecting on. In a dialogue, Su Heng, Chairperson of the Cross-Straits Economic and Trade Exchange Association, shared her first visit to the Pearl River waterfront, where she saw a bustling, prosperous scene. She noted a stark contrast: back home in Taiwan region, mainstream reports repeatedly claim that the mainland's economy is "collapsing." Why is there such a stark difference? Taiwan journalists covering APEC in Shenzhen offer a clear lens to examine this information gap. Reporters from China Times and United Daily News documented life scenes in the city, from robots making coffee to drones delivering takeout. Autonomous taxis could be seen navigating the streets, while service robots were a common sight. In Shenzhen, technologies once confined to laboratories are being transformed into practical applications that are increasingly accessible to ordinary people. However, audiences in Taiwan do not always receive the same story. Some "pan-green" media outlets disparaged Shenzhen's cityscape and focused on reports of robots malfunctioning. This contrast reflects Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' manipulation of public opinion. Taiwan singer and songwriter Lo Ta-yu criticized the DPP authorities in a recent radio interview, saying they had become a source of fear among Taiwan residents and are contributing to a decline in the island's cultural environment. His remarks have sparked widespread discussion on both sides of the Taiwan Straits. Chen Binhua, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, stated clearly that the DPP authorities push "cultural Taiwan independence" for political gain, creating "green terror" and a chilling effect. These actions hurt the interests of Taiwan compatriots and spark widespread discontent. The truth is not allowed to be heard because the DPP fears Taiwan residents will embrace joint development with the mainland. As Zhang Wensheng, deputy dean and a professor at the Taiwan Research Institute of Xiamen University, told the Global Times, "pan‑green media and commentators have long smeared the mainland, portraying it as backward and closed. This narrative feeds the false sense of superiority held by 'Taiwan independence' separatist forces, built on biased imagination." Such superiority, founded on distortion and lies, collapses when faced with real‑world facts. Cooperation opportunities abound, while the authorities keep erecting cognitive barriers. This contradiction also shows in Taiwan authorities' APEC arrangements. Lai Ching-te once again sent Stan Shih, who represented Taiwan's authorities at APEC in 2007, to this year's summit with three "mandates": participate actively in APEC affairs, advance global tech cooperation, and deepen ties with key partners. These priorities center on tech and AI supply chains. In essence, they seek to coordinate with the US to compete against the Chinese mainland in supply chains, attaching Taiwan region to Washington in APEC. However, reliance on outside forces will only marginalize Taiwan within this regional framework. The language is all about "cooperation," but behind it lies a political calculation to pursue "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces. Against this backdrop, some commentators in Taiwan region have lamented that many people on the island increasingly feel like outsiders. The Chinese mainland's vast market and innovation momentum are within reach, yet Taiwan region's public is intentionally kept away from this development arena by DPP. Taiwan region's businesspeople who came to Shenzhen for APEC have simple, practical hopes: capture gains from the mainland's high‑quality growth. Ordinary people want to work together, but the DPP authorities keep building barriers and stoking confrontation. The mainland has opened far more than just the window of this Shenzhen APEC meeting for Taiwan compatriots. It has opened the door for shared growth and mutual progress - and that door stays open. Opportunity waits right outside. Why should all Taiwan compatriots be shut out just to serve the political interests of a select few?

item.title: China prepares Shenzhou-24 mission to carry first Pakistani astronaut to space station
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 16:57:00
The Shenzhou-24 crewed spacecraft and its Long March-2F Y24 carrier rocket are transferred to the launch area at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on November 17, 2026. The mission is scheduled to be launched in the coming days, following pre-launch checks and joint tests. Photo: VCG Preparations for the upcoming Shenzhou-24 crewed mission are progressing smoothly, with winter-proofing measures, upgraded launch facilities and a backup rescue system in place as China readies for a historic joint spaceflight that will see a Pakistani astronaut become the first foreign national to visit the China Space Station. The spacecraft and its Long March-2F carrier rocket are currently in good condition, and launch site facilities and equipment are operating normally, according to a release the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) provided to the Global Times on Tuesday. The spacecraft is scheduled for launch at an appropriate time, according to the CMSA release. The nearly 60-meter-tall spacecraft-rocket combination traveled approximately 1.5 kilometers along a seamless railway track during a vertical transfer that lasted about 90 minutes, according to China Media Group (CMG). As preparations enter their final stage, engineers at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in Northwest China's Gobi Desert are addressing the challenges posed by cold weather and conducting functional inspections and joint testing ahead of liftoff. The launch center has also introduced equipment upgrades to improve operational reliability. Nearly 20 voltage stabilization devices have been installed on the launch tower to ensure a more stable electricity supply during propellant loading and launch operations, while propellant filling pumps that had been in service for more than two decades have been replaced, the state broadcaster revealed. Meanwhile, a separate spacecraft-rocket combination is already standing by as part of China's emergency rescue arrangements for crewed space missions. The Long March-2F Y25 rocket and Shenzhou-25 spacecraft have been placed on standby inside the vertical assembly building, space expert Yang Yuguang noted when interviewed by the state broadcaster. Should an emergency arise involving the Shenzhou-24 crew in orbit, the backup system is designed to enable rapid testing and transfer of the rescue spacecraft and rocket, allowing China to launch an emergency rescue mission within a relatively short period, according to CMG. Pang Zhihao, a Beijing-based senior space expert, told the Global Times on Wednesday that the preparations demonstrate the comprehensive safety measures supporting the mission, while the successful transfer of the spacecraft and rocket provides an important foundation for subsequent joint testing and functional checks. The temperature at the launch site is expected to be around 1 C during the transfer, with northwesterly winds, according to the CMG report on Wednesday. Pang said that the preparations are supported by a combination of passive thermal insulation and active heating measures designed to protect the rocket and spacecraft from low temperatures. The launch tower is equipped with enclosed protective structures and heating systems that continuously supply temperature-controlled air to the rocket's fairing and body, while insulation materials are applied to critical components, Pang explained. Additional temperature-control systems are installed around propellant tanks and engine components to ensure that sensitive equipment remains within appropriate operating ranges. "The launch procedures have also been optimized to delay the opening of the tower's rotating platforms and minimize the time the rocket and spacecraft are exposed to low temperatures," Pang told the Global Times. These measures, along with real-time meteorological monitoring and contingency plans for extreme cold, are intended to prevent temperature-related abnormalities in electronic components and propellants, ensuring the safety and reliability of the launch, he said. A Pakistani astronaut is expected to participate in the mission as a payload specialist and will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft after completing a short-term stay in orbit. The Pakistani astronaut will be the first foreign astronaut to step into China's space station, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun highlighted during a regular press conference on November 9. This marks yet another key outcome of bilateral cooperation as the two countries mark the 75th anniversary of China-Pakistan diplomatic ties, he noted. Looking ahead to the upcoming mission, Pang expressed hope that Shenzhou-24 would achieve a successful launch and safe in-orbit operations, with Chinese and foreign astronauts working closely together to carry out scientific experiments and extravehicular activities. He also voiced expectations that the Pakistani payload specialist would successfully conduct scientific research aboard the China Space Station. "The mission is expected to yield valuable scientific data and open a new chapter in international cooperation aboard the China Space Station, as China continues to embrace an open and collaborative approach to exploring the vast universe," Pang told the Global Times. Adding a human dimension to this historic mission, both Pakistani astronauts shortlisted for the mission have previously studied Chinese at the Confucius Institute in Islamabad, according to a recent report published by China News Service. Qu Zhaowei, Secretary of the Party Committee of Beijing Language and Culture University, revealed the information in an exclusive interview with China News Service on November 13 during the 2026 World Chinese Language Conference. "Both astronauts previously studied Chinese at the Confucius Institute in Islamabad," Qu said. Describing their journey from Chinese language classrooms to the prospect of traveling into space as both meaningful and inspiring, Qu said the experience demonstrates how Chinese is increasingly becoming a bridge connecting knowledge, technology, innovation and humanity's future. Qu noted that language proficiency is particularly important in highly specialized fields such as aerospace, where accurately understanding technical concepts, professional instructions and operational procedures is essential. The two candidates' experience reflects how Chinese language education is expanding beyond everyday communication into increasingly sophisticated areas of international scientific and technological cooperation, he said.
